Purpose and exclusions

Authored configuration for Content versions, schema migrations and patch compatibility. Runtime state never resides on this instance.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Select DA_ContentVersion_Development in Content Browser; set DefinitionId to a stable domain ID, then set the fields in the linked feature contract.
  2. Assign this instance to the consuming native owner through its Blueprint child/defaults or catalog; a content file that is never assigned has no runtime effect.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Author and validate stable definition/frame/field identity before use; load through declared references at readiness.
  2. Consumers may cache read-only references for their world/session lifetime; do not mutate the shared definition or place player quantities on it.
  3. On reimport/version change validate compatibility and migrate persistent IDs deliberately. Missing required rules fail closed; missing cosmetic layers use documented fallback.
  4. World/pawn teardown releases runtime references; persistent records retain IDs and versions only. Reconnect resolves the same definition without replaying grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Content versions, schema migrations and patch compatibility. Rule owner: URPGContentVersionGate. This asset’s role is Authored configuration for Content versions, schema migrations and patch compatibility. Runtime state never resides on this instance.

  1. Assign stable semantic definition IDs independent of Content Browser file names and never recycle an old ID for a different item.
  2. Author a migration with preconditions, data transformation, uniqueness checks, estimated lock/downtime and forward-recovery plan. Test on a restored staging copy.
  3. Backend records each migration transaction/version and rejects incompatible servers until the catalog/schema set is supported.
  4. At login/transfer, validate protocol, content and record versions before possession. Resolve reviewed redirects; quarantine unknown/inconsistent records for repair instead of granting default replacements repeatedly.
  5. Deploy backward-compatible expand changes first, update services/servers/clients, migrate data, and contract old columns only after rollback window ends.
  6. Patch acceptance replays old quest/inventory/skill/fishing receipts and verifies no duplicate reward, changed GUID or lost currency.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_NetworkLab / schema-v1 and schema-v2 disposable databases. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Unknown item ID -> quarantine/report while retaining owned record; no silent deletion or repeated compensation.
Migration interrupted before commit -> old schema/data remain or resumable explicit migration state; rerun does not double-transform.
Client catalog newer/older unsupported -> PatchRequired before live zone admission.
Redirect cycle -> content validation fails.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not put mutable stock, current health, inventory quantities or player quest progress on a shared Data Asset. A soft reference still needs validation and readiness.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
